prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a plain‑English site that teaches crypto basics, or (B) a service/educator that actually runs live trades or portfolios and publishes its real P&L (including losses)? Those are different things. Which do you want?

If you want plain‑English beginner education (concepts, how wallets/exchanges/tokens/stablecoins/DeFi work):
- Binance Academy — free, very beginner friendly, short articles and videos. Good plain English.
- Coin Bureau (website + YouTube) — long, clear explainers aimed at beginners and intermediate users.
- Kraken Learn Center and Coinbase Learn — exchange-run but good, straightforward primers.
- Investopedia’s crypto section — clear, non‑technical finance framing.

If you want data‑driven sites that show “real numbers” (market caps, on‑chain metrics, charts) but aren’t trading services:
- Glassnode and Coin Metrics — on‑chain/market data with transparent charts and metrics.
- Messari — research + datasets, useful for fundamentals and numbers.
- CoinGecko / CoinMarketCap — simple, beginner friendly market numbers and historical data.

If what you actually want is a teacher/service that runs live strategies and transparently publishes its trades, returns and losses (so you can see both wins and drawdowns):
- eToro (CopyTrader) — social trading platform where traders’ historical performance (P&L, wins, losses, drawdowns) is visible; you can copy them or study their records. Probably the most beginner‑friendly place to see real, public trade histories.
- Some copy‑trading or signal marketplaces (Covesting, Zignaly, Mudrex) also show past performance and loss history for strategy providers — but check how performance is verified.
- Look for educators who keep an open public spreadsheet or GitHub repo with live P&L — those are rare but much more transparent than typical influencers. If you want, I can look up a few individual traders/creators with publicly traceable track records.

A few tips no matter which route you choose:
- Don’t trust “backtests” or cherry‑picked time windows; prefer live verified track records.
- Look for third‑party verification (exchange account screenshots are weak — better are copy‑trading profiles, on‑chain wallets, or audited performance reports).
- Be skeptical of anyone who only publishes gains and hides losses.

If you tell me whether you mean education vs. transparent traders, and whether you prefer articles vs. videos vs. live P&L, I’ll give a short ranked list tailored to that.
